info.name: University Record Service
info.description:
University Record through the Gateway where the Gateway serves it, otherwise on the instance itself. base_url is {{gateway}}/api/v1/university-record: since the Gateway's 4.0.0 (#110) it serves only the player route GET /records/{category} and the public GET /health of this service, and answers 404 on every other one. A player's request names the player in X-Player-Id, which the collection pre-request script turns into a signed Bearer JWT on a Gateway request. Run the 'scenario' folder top to bottom.

LAB 4 (4.0.0). applicant.initialized, session.started and session.ended arrive from the Message Broker (topics events.<event_type>), not on POST /events, which is removed; this service's own applicant.initialized is published to events.applicant.initialized. Postman cannot send the broker's gRPC calls: the events of the scenario have to be published to the broker with the full envelope first (docs/UNIVERSITY_RECORD_SERVICE.md, §11), and the session's scopes are set with the session-service mock (POST /admin/sessions/{id}/scopes).

DIRECT CALLS. Every request whose route is not a Gateway route goes to one instance directly through {{university_record_direct_url}}, with the service's own path (/api/v1/..., /health/ready, /status, /logs, /metrics; no /university-record prefix): /health/ready, /status, /logs, /metrics, the scenario's step 4 (POST /admin/sessions/{id}/scopes) and step 9 (GET /applicants/{id}/records), POST /events, POST /applicants/next, every /admin/* request and the player-id-on-a-service-only-route edge case. The contract routes validate no token; GET /logs and, from 4.0.1 (#151), /admin/* and /dev/* check X-Service-Token themselves, so every direct request to them sends {{service_token}} (403 SERVICE_TOKEN_REQUIRED without it, 401 INVALID_SERVICE_TOKEN when wrong; the auth edge cases have both on an admin route). Through the broker /admin/* and /dev/* cannot be reached, since the broker never passes the token on. A direct service call on a contract route carries no X-Service-Token and no X-Player-Id, and a direct request that plays a player sends X-Player-Id as it is (the pre-request script signs no JWT and changes no header of a direct request). Direct and Gateway requests must reach the same database: in the team stack forward an instance's port (docs/UNIVERSITY_RECORD_SERVICE.md, §11).

RUN FROM POSTMAN ON THE TEAM STACK. The compose publishes no port of this service (2 instances), so {{university_record_direct_url}} (localhost:8084) answers only while one instance is forwarded to this machine:
docker run --rm -d --name university-record-direct --network student-id-net -p 127.0.0.1:8084:8080 alpine/socat TCP-LISTEN:8080,fork,reuseaddr TCP:university-record-service:8080
Bound to 127.0.0.1 only; stop it when done: docker stop university-record-direct. Set service_token and jwt_secret to SERVICE_TOKEN and JWT_SECRET of the stack's .env. Checked on 2026-11-13 against the team stack this way.

LAB 5 (5.0.0, #176). session.started is retired: the juniors' scopes arrive as the input of the saga step grant-scopes of shift.start, which the broker's coordinator calls (POST /api/v1/saga-steps/grant-scopes and .../compensate, service-only, not Gateway routes). The folder 'Saga step grant-scopes (direct, inside the network)' calls them directly on an instance, and the scenario's step 4a sets its scopes with them. Both read the instance version from GET /status first and skip the saga requests on a 4.x instance (the console says why), where step 4 sets the scopes with the session-service mock (POST /admin/sessions/{id}/scopes) instead.

variable.description: The instance itself, not the Gateway: its port is not published in the team stack, so forward one instance there (docker run --rm -d --name university-record-direct --network student-id-net -p 127.0.0.1:8084:8080 alpine/socat TCP-LISTEN:8080,fork,reuseaddr TCP:university-record-service:8080), bound to this machine only and stopped after the demo, since the instance trusts X-Player-Id as it comes; it shares the stack's database with the Gateway requests, or run the service's own compose (APP_HOST_PORT, 8084 by default) for the direct requests alone.
The stack's SERVICE_TOKEN; sent as X-Service-Token on the direct GET /logs and, from 4.0.1, /admin/* and /dev/* requests, the routes the instance checks it on. The contract routes check no token
Set by the version requests from GET /status; the saga step requests (5.0.0) are skipped below 5

exec: // Through the Gateway a player is identified by a JWT (HS256, JWT_SECRET shared with Player Service),
// never by X-Player-Id: the Gateway checks the token, discards any client-sent X-Player-Id and sets
// its own from the token's sub. This script signs the token itself: every request that names a
// player in X-Player-Id gets Authorization: Bearer <jwt> with sub = that id, and the X-Player-Id
// A direct request ({{university_record_direct_url}}) reaches the instance itself, which reads
// X-Player-Id as it is and no JWT: it keeps the header and gets no token.
// jwt_secret must equal JWT_SECRET of the Gateway in the stack's .env.
const unsigned = part({ alg: 'HS256', typ: 'JWT' }) + '.' + part({ sub: sub, iat: now, exp: now + 300 });

scenario - honest student, identity theft, scopes, session end
item.description:
From 4.0.0 the events of this scenario arrive from the Message Broker, which Postman cannot call, so they are not requests here any more. Publish them to the broker with the full envelope (docs/UNIVERSITY_RECORD_SERVICE.md, §11) at the missing step numbers: 3 applicant.initialized of the honest FAF student (applicant {{honest_applicant_id}}, actual student_id FAF23117, name Ana Rusu) before step 5; 8 applicant.initialized of an outsider claiming FAF23117 (applicant {{thief_applicant_id}}) before step 9; 10 session.ended of {{session_id}} before step 11. The checks 4b, 8 and 10 ask the service whether each event arrived; without it, the step that needs it (5, 9, 11) is skipped, not failed, and the console says why. Step 4 sets the scopes with the session-service mock in place of session.started. Steps 4 and 9 are service calls on routes the Gateway's 4.0.0 does not serve (404), so they go to the instance directly ({{university_record_direct_url}}, no X-Player-Id; step 4, an /admin/* route, sends X-Service-Token: {{service_token}} from 4.0.1, step 9 no token); steps 5, 6, 7 and 11 are the player route, through the Gateway with the JWT. Both must reach the same database (forward an instance of the team stack, docs/UNIVERSITY_RECORD_SERVICE.md, §11).

0 reads the instance version. On 5.x step 4a sets the scopes with the saga step grant-scopes (session.started is retired) and step 4 is skipped; on 4.x step 4 sets them with the session-service mock and step 4a is skipped. Steps 4 and 9 are service calls on routes the Gateway's 4.0.0 does not serve (404), so they go to the instance directly ({{university_record_direct_url}}, no X-Player-Id; step 4, an /admin/* route, sends X-Service-Token: {{service_token}} from 4.0.1, step 9 no token); steps 5, 6, 7 and 11 are the player route, through the Gateway with the JWT. Both must reach the same database (forward an instance of the team stack, docs/UNIVERSITY_RECORD_SERVICE.md, §11).

item.name: events - they come from the broker (Lab 4)
item.description: From 4.0.0 applicant.initialized, session.started and session.ended are delivered by the Message Broker (topics events.<event_type>) and settled with Ack OK / PERMANENT / RETRY; POST /events is removed. The old cases of this folder are now Ack outcomes: a repeated event_id is OK (duplicate); an unknown event_type, an unknown version or a profile nested under a 'profile' key is PERMANENT (the old 422 INVALID_EVENT), and the broker dead-letters it (docs/UNIVERSITY_RECORD_SERVICE.md, §6 and §11). The request below goes to the instance directly, so the 404 is the service's own (the route is removed), not the Gateway's 4.0.0, which answers 404 on it as well.

item.description: The three requests on GET /records/{category} go through the Gateway: without X-Player-Id the collection signs no JWT and the Gateway answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; with 'not-a-uuid' the JWT's sub is not a player id and the Gateway answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; an unknown category passes the Gateway (the route matches any category) and the service answers 422. The service-only-route cases go to the instance directly, since the Gateway's 4.0.0 answers 404 on /admin/* before any credential: with X-Player-Id as it is and the right {{service_token}}, the service answers 403 SERVICE_TOKEN_REQUIRED to a player on a service-only route (the token does not make a player's request a service call); from 4.0.1 (#151) without X-Service-Token it answers 403 SERVICE_TOKEN_REQUIRED and with a wrong one 401 INVALID_SERVICE_TOKEN.

Saga step grant-scopes (direct, inside the network)
item.description: LAB 5 (5.0.0, #176). Step 2 of the saga shift.start: POST /api/v1/saga-steps/grant-scopes stores each junior's record_scopes for the session, POST /api/v1/saga-steps/grant-scopes/compensate deletes the session and its scopes (docs/UNIVERSITY_RECORD_SERVICE.md, section 13). The broker's saga coordinator calls them as service calls on requests.university-record; the Gateway does not route them (404, see the auth edge cases). Here they go to one instance directly ({{university_record_direct_url}}) as the coordinator would send them: no X-Player-Id. The service checks no token on them; the first request sends X-Service-Token anyway to show it is ignored. Idempotent by (saga_id, step); the pre-request scripts make fresh UUIDs, so the folder can run again. Request 0 reads the instance version from GET /status: on a 4.x instance (no saga routes) every other request is skipped, not failed, and the console says why. Run the folder top to bottom.
